page.layout: One column of verse, set in italic, with a centred running head above it. Below the text, on the right, the last line "Militiæ," is set flush right. No page number, catchword or signature is printed. No marginal notes.

l.i: Vt leuis in Naphtham sulco volat alite flamma;
Séque choris alacres tandem felicibus addunt:
Et tandem felix Studijs concordibus ævum
Lætæ agitant duce cum CHRISTO, viuáque fruuntur
Luce Dei, coràmque illum immensumque tuuntur[?]
Luminis æterni fontem, vitæque beatæ
Diuitias, pedibúsque polos & sydera calcant.
At vero nocti sempérque silentibus umbris
Iam mersos & densa olim caligine condi,
Atque adeo illorum cineres, famámque profundis
Obduca[?] tenebris, & ferro & carcere dudum
Rebare[?] extinctam flammisque voracibus haustam.
Sed cælo visum est aliter; namque incubat istis
Fama ingens tumulis, quæ sese ex ossibus ultrix
Protulit innocuæ gentis, latéque per omnes
Vulgavit populos, ingenti maxima plausu
Egregias animas, nolit velit ægra tyrannis
Roma tua, & cineri dat splendida nomina muto.
Ergo agedum illustres animæ, vos posthuma fama
E[?] nocte & tenebris, ad vitæ & luminis auras
Ecce tubæ revocat sonitu officiosa potenti
Emerentis[?] sanctéque pio certamine functas.
Vos Pater amplexu non dedignatus amico,
Arbitrio[?] fati exemptas Regumque furori
In cælum Pater omnipotens excepit ouantes.
Quare agitè & sacris etiamnum accentibus
omnes Inumerum[?], densæ toto date carmina cælo;
Cælo ubi perpetuas alas chorus haurit anhelans
Delicias, paræque bibunt noua gaudia mentes:
Gaudia nil humile, aut fluxum spirantia porrò,
Gaudia parta piis atque obseruantibus æqui.
Vestra sed hæc olim memores exempla sequuti
Sic cælum repetant gratíque pùque[?] nepotes,
Qui dederint vltro durae sua nomina CHRISTI
Militiæ,

page.notes: Several words are uncertain because of the print and the scan: "Rebare", "Obduca", "Emerentis", "Arbitrio", "Inumerum", "pùque" and "tuuntur" are marked [?]. The initial "E" of "E nocte" is also uncertain. Long s has been transcribed as s throughout, so "sulco" appears where the scan looks like "fulco". The line "Militiæ," is a right-aligned continuation of the last stanza, so it is included with it.
